description: Reorganize the registry under assets/, add local-only scaffold commands for skills and agents.md integrations, and add Codebuff as a fourth supported harness alongside Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.

userStories.title: Relocate skills/ and agents.md/ under assets/
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the registry content under assets/ so the repo root is clearer and code is separated from data.
acceptanceCriteria: `git mv skills assets/skills` and `git mv agents.md assets/agents.md` so history is preserved
Every existing entry (grill-me, storytelling-mastery-skill, write-a-skill, karpathy-guidelines) is present under the new path with all its files intact
mapping.yml install_path values are rewritten in the same commit: `skills/<name>/` -> `assets/skills/<name>/` and `agents.md/<name>/` -> `assets/agents.md/<name>/`

`grep -rn '^skills/\|^agents\.md/\|"skills/\|"agents\.md/' --exclude-dir=target --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=assets --exclude-dir=archive` returns no matches outside intentional documentation history
docs/manifest-schema.md and docs/mapping-schema.md update every example path to the new `assets/...` prefix
README.md `## Repository layout` tree shows `assets/skills/` and `assets/agents.md/`
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: cargo build is intentionally broken between US-001 and US-002 per the PRD's technical considerations (the build.rs path constants are updated in US-002).

userStories.title: Update build.rs to scan assets/ for manifests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the offline-catalog build to read manifests from the new assets/ paths so cargo build still works after the move.
acceptanceCriteria: src/external/build.rs reads `assets/skills/*/manifest.yml` and `assets/agents.md/*/manifest.yml` instead of the previous top-level paths
Cargo rerun-if-changed directives reference the new `assets/` paths so edits there still trigger rebuilds
`cargo build` from the repo root succeeds on a clean checkout after US-001
`cargo test -p instinctagents` (or workspace equivalent) passes; any catalog tests that previously hard-coded `skills/` are updated
Missing or malformed manifests still fail the build with the new path in the error message
The invariant `manifest.name == parent folder basename` is still enforced (basename did not change; only the parent prefix moved)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Centralize assets/ paths in src/internal/lib.py
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the internal Python scripts to write into assets/ via centralized constants so every ingest / list / remove command keeps working.
acceptanceCriteria: Path helpers in src/internal/lib.py (entry_dir, install_path_for, and any constants like SKILLS_DIR / AGENTS_MD_DIR) return `assets/skills/<name>/` and `assets/agents.md/<name>/`
No script under src/internal/ hard-codes the literal strings `skills/` or `agents.md/` for registry paths -- all go through the lib helpers
End-to-end smoke test: `uv run --project src/internal python src/internal/skill_list.py` succeeds and reports the four existing entries with the new install_paths
End-to-end smoke test: re-running `skill_add` against an already-installed entry with `--force` still works (writes back into `assets/skills/<name>/`)
`skill_remove` and `agents_md_remove` successfully delete a test entry under `assets/...` and rewrite `mapping.yml`
ruff (or whichever linter src/internal/ already uses) passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add Codebuff variant to the Harness enum and detection
userStories.description: As a Codebuff user, I want instinctagents to detect my project as Codebuff so installs land in the right place.
acceptanceCriteria: src/external/src/harness.rs adds `Harness::Codebuff` enum variant
`Harness::Codebuff::target_folder()` returns `.agents/skills/`
`Harness::Codebuff::agents_md_file()` returns `AGENTS.md`
`detect()` checks Codebuff LAST, after ClaudeCode -> Codex -> OpenCode; signals are: `.agents/` directory OR `knowledge.md` file at the project root

New unit tests: detect via `.agents/` dir alone, detect via `knowledge.md` alone, priority test where `CLAUDE.md` + `.agents/` resolves as ClaudeCode, priority test where `AGENTS.md` + `.agents/` resolves as Codex, and target_folder / agents_md_file value checks
All existing harness.rs tests still pass
`cargo test` passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Accept `codebuff` as a manifest harness_compatibility value
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to tag a skill or integration as Codebuff-compatible in its manifest.
acceptanceCriteria: build.rs manifest validation accepts `codebuff` as a fourth valid `harness_compatibility` value alongside `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`
An invalid value (e.g. `cursor`) still fails the build with a clear error naming the offending manifest path
docs/manifest-schema.md lists `codebuff` in the allowed values section and in the example with harness restriction
At least one new test (in build.rs or catalog.rs) covers a manifest with `harness_compatibility: [codebuff]` and asserts it parses successfully
`cargo build` and `cargo test` pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Wire Codebuff through the installer and TUI compatibility filter
userStories.description: As a Codebuff user, I want the TUI Add tab to show me Codebuff-compatible entries and install them into .agents/skills/.
acceptanceCriteria: src/external/src/installer.rs uses `Harness::Codebuff::target_folder()` and `agents_md_file()` -- no Codebuff-specific branching outside the enum
TUI Add tab dim/disable filter treats Codebuff the same as other harnesses: rows with non-empty `harness_compatibility` that excludes `codebuff` are dimmed when Codebuff is detected
`--force` flag still allows installing an incompatible entry into a Codebuff project
TUI status area reports Codebuff when running inside a fixture dir containing only `.agents/`
Manual smoke test (documented in the commit message or progress.txt): build the binary, run in a temp dir with `.agents/`, install one existing entry, verify it landed in `.agents/skills/<name>/`
`cargo test` passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add prompt_multi_choice helper to src/internal/lib.py
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a reusable multi-select prompt helper so the scaffold commands can collect harness_compatibility from the user.
acceptanceCriteria: src/internal/lib.py exposes `prompt_multi_choice(prompt: str, options: list[str]) -> list[str]` that prompts on a TTY and returns the user's selected subset (empty list = no selection)
Function uses the same I/O patterns as the existing `prompt_choice` / `prompt_text` helpers (stdin/stdout, non-TTY raises a clear error rather than silently defaulting)
Input parsing accepts comma-separated indices (e.g. `1,3`) or comma-separated labels; whitespace tolerant; empty input yields an empty list
Invalid input re-prompts rather than crashing
Unit test (in src/internal/, alongside any existing tests) covers: empty input, single selection, multiple selection, invalid then valid re-prompt
ruff passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add `skill-new <name>` scaffold command
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to run `skill-new my-skill` and have the CLI prompt for the manifest fields so I can create a local-only skill entry.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/internal/skill_new.py with `main(argv)` entrypoint mirroring the shape of skill_add.py
Accepts one positional arg `<name>` and a `--force` flag

Prompts for: description (required, non-empty string), version (default `0.1.0`, must parse as semver), harness_compatibility (multi-select from claude-code / codex / opencode / codebuff via the US-007 helper; empty = all harnesses)
Sanitizes the input name via existing `sanitize_name` helper and writes the entry to `assets/skills/<name>/`
Generated files: `manifest.yml` (with all entered fields, `name` matching the sanitized arg) and `SKILL.md` containing `# <name>` plus a single `TODO: describe the skill` line
Appends to mapping.yml under `installed_skills` with `source_url: local` and `install_path: assets/skills/<name>/`
Refuses to clobber an existing entry (folder on disk OR mapping entry) without `--force`; with `--force` overwrites both
Non-TTY invocation fails with a clear error message (matching skill_add.py's --as flag pattern)

Slash-command wrappers created under `.claude/commands/skill-new.md`, `.codex/skills/skill-new/SKILL.md`, and `.opencode/commands/skill-new.md`, each delegating to `uv run --project src/internal python src/internal/skill_new.py $ARGUMENTS`
ruff passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add `agents-md-new <name>` scaffold command
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the same interactive scaffold for agents.md integrations so I can author a new snippet locally.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/internal/agents_md_new.py with `main(argv)` entrypoint mirroring agents_md_add.py
Accepts one positional arg `<name>` and a `--force` flag
Prompts for the same field set as US-008: description, version (default 0.1.0, semver-validated), harness_compatibility (multi-select including codebuff)
Writes `assets/agents.md/<name>/manifest.yml` and `assets/agents.md/<name>/snippet.md` containing `# <name>` plus a single `TODO: describe the integration` line
Appends to mapping.yml under `installed_agents_md` with `source_url: local` and `install_path: assets/agents.md/<name>/`
Refuses to clobber an existing entry without `--force`
Non-TTY invocation fails with a clear error message
Slash-command wrappers created under `.claude/commands/agents-md-new.md`, `.codex/skills/agents-md-new/SKILL.md`, and `.opencode/commands/agents-md-new.md`
ruff passes
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Update README and slash-command docs for Codebuff and scaffold commands

acceptanceCriteria: README.md harness list updates to: `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `OpenCode`, and `Codebuff`
README.md harness-detection paragraph mentions the `.agents/` / `knowledge.md` signals and notes Codebuff is matched LAST
README.md `## For maintainers` section documents `/skill-new` and `/agents-md-new` alongside `/skill-add` and `/agents-md-add`, with a one-line description of each

If a top-level CHANGELOG or release-notes file exists, an entry is added; otherwise skip silently
